extraction.Name: Maggie Salway, nee Ladeaux
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent in fee to her 160 acre allotment when it was issued, April 13,1918, but she was told by the Indian Agency that, if she did not accept it, and pay the taxes on her land, it would be taxed just the same, for which it would later be sold, so she accepted it
extraction.Buyer: sold her allotment to her step-father, Arthur R. Van Wert, of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, for $1400.00, paying $400.00 in cash, and he gave her an automobile and 18 head of mares, which trade they valued at $1000.00
extraction.Occupation/Income: her husband supports the family by clerking in a general store, in Pine Ridge, South Dakota; and that this is their only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, good health; married and mother of four minor children; one child, 10 years old, has lung trouble and loses time out of school, but the other three children are healthy; husband's health is good; she considers that she received a good price for her allotment; did not sell her allotment for any debts incurred prior to receiving her patent in fee; has never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; affidavit sworn March 6, 1929; document also contains a separate affidavit for Lizzie Shangreau (No. 3596)
